display.title: Episode 391: The Sound of the Shofar (Shabbos Mevarchim Elul)
display.summary_short: Before Elul, Uncle Yossi explains the King in the Field, and tells of a village boy who thought a fire bugle puts out fires: the shofar is a call to action.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week of Shabbos Mevarchim Elul 5749. Uncle Yossi prepares listeners to welcome the greatest King: he teaches two words, 'Melech BaSadeh', and retells the Alter Rebbe's parable from Likkutei Torah of a king returning to his city, who greets everyone in the fields with a radiant face and grants their requests, unlike in his palace, where few may enter. So it is in Elul, when Hashem is close to every Jew. Children should make a long list of requests, with Moshiach at the top, since the Rebbe said the coming year 5750 stands for 'a year of miracles'. After a lively Hakochainik march, a yeshiva boy recites the Shema. Since the shofar is blown every weekday in Elul, the story tells of a village plagued by fires that sends a farm boy to the city to learn what is done there. He sees the fire chief blow a bugle from a tower and brings one home, but when fire breaks out his loud blowing does nothing. The chief explains that the bugle only alarms people to fetch water. So too, the shofar wakes us to act with teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah. The show ends with the sponsor and candle-lighting time.
display.lesson: The shofar is an alarm, not the solution: it calls us to do teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah.

date.note: 'This coming Shabbos is Shabbos Mevarchim Elul' (26 Aug 1989, Re'eh); candle time 7:19; weekly after 390 (15 Aug).

advisories.note: Fires repeatedly burn down homes in a village, leaving people homeless.

sources_cited.note: The parable of the King in the Field (Melech BaSadeh) for the month of Elul.
The letters of the year 5750 stand for 'it will be a year of miracles'.

segments.title: Melech BaSadeh: the King in the Field
segments.summary: The Alter Rebbe's parable: in Elul Hashem is like a king in the field who greets everyone and grants their requests.

segments.title: The Sound of the Shofar
segments.summary: A farm boy learns that a fire bugle only sounds the alarm; the shofar likewise calls us to act.
